$schema_note: Hosts the bench-fleet study covers. ssh_alias must be resolvable from Tower2 via ~/.ssh/config. local=true means run commands directly with bash, not via ssh. Each host lists the backends to build + bench.

bonus_model.name: qwen3-coder-next
bonus_model.notes: Large MoE, Q8_0 is a split-file set. Bonus study, Blackwell-only. Spark aarch64 has a separate garbage-token bug — try then document.

m5_room.circuit: separate 20 A breaker (different room, isolated to avoid trips)

m5_mbp.note: MBP exhaust essentially room-temperature — laptop cooling has massive headroom on this workload

tower2.note: Workstation tower with 14× Noctua 120 mm + open panel — exhaust at room temperature, cooling system massively over-provisioned

spark.note: DGX Spark compact desktop chassis pushing 40°F above ambient at sustained load

strix_halo.note: GMKtec EVO X2 NUC-class chassis pushing 60°F above ambient — small surface area limit visible, consistent with sustained 98°C edge sensor readings

environment.interpretation: Tower2 and M5 are exhausting essentially room temperature air despite running the same workload at much higher silicon power than Strix/Spark — their cooling systems are sized for the workload, not stressed by it. Spark's compact-desktop chassis works moderately hard (40°F delta). Strix's NUC-class chassis is the limiting factor (60°F delta, chassis surface area is the binding constraint, not silicon). This is the chassis-class story the headline thermal data implies.

hosts.name: tower2
hosts.chassis: Custom workstation tower (ASUS WRX90E, 1600 W titanium PSU, 8× Noctua 120 mm intake + 6× exhaust = 14-fan airflow, open-air panel)
hosts.cpu: AMD Threadripper PRO 7965WX (24 cores / 48 threads, 350 W rated TDP)
hosts.gpus: 2× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation (96 GB GDDR7 each). gpu0 is the bench GPU at 600 W cap; gpu1 idles during the cross-host run (~17 W board) but is present and contributing to wall draw.

cost_usd_approx.as_configured_note: Built ground-up as a 1600 W professional dual-GPU inference server: TR PRO CPU, server-grade WRX90E board, ECC RAM (2×+ vs standard), 1600 W titanium PSU, redundant cooling. Most of the over-spec is for dual-GPU + workstation reliability, not for cross-host inference comparison.
cost_usd_approx.reasonable_build_note: What a fair cross-host comparison should anchor on — same gpu0 silicon, consumer/prosumer parts elsewhere. Performs the same on single-GPU inference workloads; the rest of the workstation overhead is configuration choice, not inference requirement. Anchored at $12k (deliberately on the generous side — covers a quality consumer board, capable PSU, decent cooling, NVMe, and quality RAM, with margin) so the comparison doesn't underestimate the discrete-GPU build cost.

system_overhead_breakdown_at_compute_lig.note: Workstation 'presence tax' is ~150–200 W even before GPU work starts. Important context for any wall-AC efficiency comparison against laptop/NUC-class hosts.

single_gpu_equivalent_calibration.rationale: To compare Tower2 fairly against single-GPU hosts (M5, Spark, Strix), subtract gpu1's idle contribution from the wall reading. gpu1 idle is measured at 16.1 W (mean, range 13.7-20.8 W) — not 50 W; that higher number applies to active/warm-clocked states, not P8 idle.
single_gpu_equivalent_calibration.m5_to_tower2_efficiency_ratio_single_gpu: M5 wins by ~1.46× at wall AC for a single-RTX-6000 comparison (vs ~1.61× dual-GPU)

wall_calibration.method: permanent dedicated plug meter on Tower2 outlet

data_point_1.system_overhead_dc_w_derived: ~207 W (CPU + RAM + chipset + fans + NVMe + misc, after 94% PSU efficiency)
data_point_1.note: This is a compute-light cell so wall efficiency at this cell is low; need a peak-cell reading (ctx=1024 conc=8 gen=2048) for the honest cross-host efficiency comparison.

wall_calibration.still_needed: Wall reading at peak silicon cell (ctx=1024 conc=8 gen=2048). The 27B leg's peak cells completed early in the run before plug-meter calibration; will recapture during Tower2's 35B-A3B leg which re-runs short-ctx high-conc cells.

hosts.notes: 2× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation (96 GB each, GDDR7). For the parallel cross-host run, ONLY GPU 0 is used (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0) at 600W cap — keeps the room breaker safe when all four hosts run concurrently. GPU 0 600W ≈ 5090 575W TGP, so single-card numbers read across to a 5090 within a few percent (excluding VRAM-ceiling effects: 32GB on 5090 vs 96GB on PRO 6000). Dual-card supplementary run executes SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel sweep clears. dream-llama-server must be stopped before bench runs. M5 is in a different room — not on the same breaker.

hosts.name: strix-halo
hosts.chassis: GMKtec EVO X2 mini-PC (NUC-class small-form-factor enclosure)
hosts.cost_note: GMKtec EVO X2 retail as of 2026-05-15.
hosts.broken_rocm_finding: PRELIMINARY (single-attempt) — ROCm 6.4.4 (libamdhip64.so.6.4.60404) failed to bring llama-server to a ready state on Qwen3.6-27B-Q8 load in our one smoke cell. Detailed failure mode (offset 0x3a4e52 / fault addr 0x18, HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION tries) was logged opportunistically and not yet re-verified with longer wait-ready, smaller model, or fresh stderr/dmesg capture. Vulkan backend works fine on the same hardware. Until a proper retry sub-study with longer wait-ready, smaller bootstrap, and fresh stderr/dmesg capture completes, treat 'ROCm broken on Strix Halo' as unconfirmed — the published study claim is Vulkan numbers only, not a comparative claim against ROCm.
hosts.thermal_sensor_caveat: rocm-smi on this kernel/driver exposes ONLY 'Temperature (Sensor edge)'. No junction sensor is exposed by the AMD kernel driver on Strix Halo. Junction is typically 10–15 °C hotter than edge.
hosts.notes: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 124 GB unified, in a GMKtec EVO X2 mini-PC chassis. Vulkan currently canonical pending ROCm retry sub-study. Form factor is a small NUC-class enclosure, NOT a workstation — compare power/thermal numbers in that light.

hosts.name: spark
hosts.chassis: NVIDIA DGX Spark reference desktop (compact desktop form factor)
hosts.notes: DGX Spark GB10 Grace Blackwell, 121 GB unified, aarch64. NOT a Jetson — tegrastats does not apply; use nvidia-smi for power+thermals same as Tower2. CUDA 13.0 at /usr/local/cuda (not in default PATH). Coder-Next has known aarch64 garbage-token bug; Qwen3.6-27B + 35B-A3B verified fine.
